title: Senate to Vote on Crypto Rules — and Trump's Billions
summary:
What if your video game coins were worth billions of dollars — and the president owned a lot of them? That's kind of the fight happening in the Senate on Tuesday. Senators will vote on whether to move forward with a bill that creates new rules for cryptocurrency, a type of digital money. The market is worth $2.3 trillion.

The vote comes just two months before the midterm elections. The crypto industry has become a major political force, and President Trump has made a lot of money from crypto while in office. Democrats say the bill doesn't do enough to stop Trump and his family from enriching themselves. "Let's make sure that we do not pass a crypto bill that will let Donald Trump continue to rake in billions of dollars in crypto profits while working families struggle," said Sen. Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts.

Trump has agreed to some concessions, including new restrictions on federal elected officials issuing digital assets like the meme coins he and his wife Melania launched. On Sunday, he agreed to give state attorneys general more power to enforce the crypto measure. But most Democrats say that's not enough. Sen. Ruben Gallego of Arizona and Sen. Thom Tillis of North Carolina wanted Trump to put his crypto holdings in a blind trust — where he can't control them — and sell them when they reach a certain value. Gallego said the latest version "leaves a lot to be desired."

Republicans need 60 votes to move forward, but the Senate is 53-47. Supporters say the bill gives the industry legal certainty and protects consumers. Opponents say it's a giveaway to an industry that spent more than $130 million in 2024 congressional races.
why_it_matters: Digital money is showing up in games, apps and online stores, so the rules lawmakers write now will shape what kids can buy, trade and use on their phones later on.

background_read: The Senate (the part of the U.S. Congress that makes laws, with 100 members — two from each state) usually needs 60 votes to move a bill forward, which is why one party often needs help from the other.
Cryptocurrency like Bitcoin (the first digital money, created in 2009) grew very fast, and governments around the world are still figuring out how to make rules for it.
Sen. Elizabeth Warren (a U.S. senator from Massachusetts known for keeping a close eye on banks and big money) is one of the bill's loudest critics.
Article_Structure: WHO: U.S. senators, President Donald Trump, Sen. Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts, Sen. Ruben Gallego of Arizona, and Sen. Thom Tillis of North Carolina.
WHAT: The Senate votes on whether to move forward with a bill that creates new rules for cryptocurrency, a market worth $2.3 trillion.
WHERE: The U.S. Senate, two months before the midterm elections, with the Senate split 53-47.
WHY: Democrats say the bill would let Trump keep making billions from crypto, while supporters say it gives the industry legal certainty and protects consumers.

perspectives.description: They say clear rules would make crypto safer for ordinary people and would stop companies from being confused about what is legal.
They worry the bill is a gift to an industry that spent more than $130 million on campaigns, and that it lets the president profit while in office.
They note that crypto is still very new and that countries everywhere are arguing about how much to regulate it.
